subject: ConditionalPanel causing plot to load multiple times

messages.author: 07ad8b37c843f326
messages.subject: ConditionalPanel causing plot to load multiple times
parts:
Hey all, 

I'm pretty new to using conditionalPanel in Shiny and I have a quick question. I have several tabs in my Shiny app. I would like to dynamically change which UI controls are visible on each tab. 

Using conditionalPanel, I am able to successfully declare which UI controls are visible on each tab. However, this causes plots on these tabs to load multiple times whenever I use one of the input controls in the conditionalPanel. I suspect Shiny is re-rendering the plot every time for each UI control in my conditional statement. This clearly a behavior that I wish to avoid. My plots are created using ggplot2 and I'm running Shiny locally. 

How can I get Shiny to render my plot only once?

Pertinent UI Code Snippet Below:

UI

 conditionalPanel(
    condition = "input.tabs1=='Football'",
      checkboxInput(inputId = "highMode",
          label = strong("Show Field in High Definition"),
          value = FALSE),
       helpText("Selecting to show field in high definition will significantly increase load time"),
       selectInput("teamName", strong("Team Selection"),
          choices = c("All" = "all",
                      "Red" = "red",
                      "Blue" = "blue"))
        # uiOutput("statCheck")

      ),

mainPanel(
    tabsetPanel(id="tabs1",

      tabPanel("Football"
        , plotOutput("teamColor", height="auto")
        , plotOutput("teamBar")
      ),

messages.author: 5712068fdf482d27
messages.subject: Re: ConditionalPanel causing plot to load multiple times
parts:
I suspect you might want to wrap all your controls in isolate in your server.R code e.g. isolate(input$something) where ever you have input$something in your server.R code. Also add a actionButton to the page and use if(input$yourActionButton >0 ) to run the code only if it's pressed. E.g.

output$something <- renderSomething({
if(input$yourActionButton > 0) {
  doSomethingWith(isloate(input$something))
  doSomethingWith(isloate(input$somethingElse))
}
})

instead of

output$something <- renderSomething({
  doSomethingWith(input$something)
  doSomethingWith1(input$somethingElse)
})

in the isolate example your output will not change until you press the yourActionButton, in the second cases whenever something or somethingElse changes your output will change
